title: Fast Recovery Patch & Rollback Matrix — runbook, branch policy, backport automation
creator: Ava Moreno
description:
Purpose: Define a pragmatic, testable fast-recovery runbook for critical regressions and outages that standardizes: severity criteria, patch-branch naming, backporting automation, CI gating, rollback vs rollforward decision factors, and post-deploy validation.

Scope: applies to hosted API and Dedicated runtime product surfaces (runtime, routing, autoscale). Excludes non-production prototypes. This is the canonical engineering-runbook for incidents that meet Severity S1 or S2 as defined below.

Goals:
- Reduce mean time to safe remediation for P0 incidents to under 60 minutes (detect->mitigate->validate->release).
- Standardize branch and backport semantics so any engineer can create a patch branch and request an expedited backport.
- Automate low-risk backports (patchlevel bumps, config flags) and gate higher-risk backports behind test windows and sign-offs.
- Minimize customer-impacting rollbacks by preferring rollforward patches when safe and fast.

Severity criteria (actionable):
- S0/Critical: Data loss or compromise, customer data integrity impacted. Immediate security playbook (security team lead).
- S1/ServiceOutage: API unavailable for >1 region or >5% of traffic error budget burned in 5m. Initiate full fast-recovery flow.
- S2/Degraded: Latency or error spike affecting a single region or single model variant where graceful degradation policies do not mitigate impact. Initiate fast patch path but allow additional testing window (30–90 min).
- S3/Minor: Regressions not causing immediate customer failures; schedule normal release lanes.

Branch and patch naming policy (machine-friendly, predictable):
- Always start from the release branch matching customer environment: release/runtime-2.3 (for LTS patching use release/runtime-2.3-lts).
- Patch branch: patch/ENG-<ticket>-<short-desc>-<semver>. Example: patch/ENG-72345-runtime-kvcache-fix-2.3.1
- Backport branch: backport/2.3/ENG-72345 or backport/lts/2.3-2026-03-13 for automated tooling to discover.
- Merge commit message template: "cherry-pick: ENG-72345 <one-line summary>"

Backport policy and automation: automated tiers
- Tier A (auto): Non-functional changes, config tweaks, feature flags, hotfixes that pass unit+integration smoke in <20m. Tooling will auto-create PRs against release branches and run the targeted fast-smoke job. If green, auto-merge with approval from on-call release engineer.
- Tier B (manual + auto-assist): Code changes touching serving runtime but not kernel selection or KV cache internals. Tooling will create PR and run extended integration (30–45m). Requires a code-owner approval; the backport bot will hold for a single 1-hour manual review window before merge.
- Tier C (manual): Kernel-level changes, changes to backward compatibility, or security patches. Requires designated release lead + security sign-off; no auto-merge. Use the emergency patch pipeline.

Rollback vs Rollforward decision matrix (fast):
- If change introduces data corruption or security exposure -> rollback immediately and trigger incident postmortem.
- If change causes availability regressions but a small, targeted fix is available and can be validated in <60m -> rollforward patch.
- If no quick patch and partial mitigation possible (traffic routing, model variant fallback) -> apply mitigation, schedule rollback only after 2h if not resolved.

Playbook steps (first 60 minutes):
1) Triage: SRE on-call labels ticket ENG-xxxx and assigns severity. Notify PM and release lead.
2) Hotfix branch creation: create patch branch from release/<branch> following naming policy. Record in ticket with GH PR link.
3) Fast-smoke CI: run smoke suite (priority smoke tests list: ingest, inference-happy-path, auth, billing hooks). If fails, rollback candidate.
4) Backport PR creation: backport bot opens backport/<branch> PRs as per tier. Tag required approvers.
5) Canary rollout: deploy to 1% of traffic for 10 minutes, monitor errors, SLOs. If green, increase to 25% then 100% with 10–15 min windows.
6) Post-verify: attach traces/dashboard snapshots, Canary metrics, and customer-facing notes. Close the loop with customer success if impacted.

CI/CD and gating:
- New fast-smoke pipeline (pipeline-fast-smoke) with 20m walltime and subset test matrix. This pipeline runs on backport PRs and hotfix branches.
- Canary automation via infra: /deploy canary --target release/2.3 --traffic 1% --tag ENG-72345. CLI returns rollout ID; merge operator monitors via rollout API.

Testing and validation:
- Maintain a canonical smoke test list in Confluence (link below). Add any new regression tests discovered in incident into the fast-smoke suite as part of the follow-up.
- For changes touching kernel selection or quantization: require performance microbenchmarks and 3-run median latency before canary progression.

Roles and responsibilities:
- SRE On-call: immediate triage, mitigation, traffic controls.
- Release Lead: authorizes rollbacks and major backports; coordinates PR approvals.
- Patch Author: creates patch branch, authors PRs, runs local repros.
- Code Owners: required approvers per CODEOWNERS for manual merges.

Post-incident actions:
- Run a 72-hour stabilization window after a hotfix where any regression triggers automatic rollback and postmortem.
- Add regression to prioritized evals and expand test coverage.
- Metrics to collect: time-to-triage, time-to-first-patch, time-to-canary-green, % rollbacks vs rollforwards, customer-impact minutes.

Risk and trade-offs:
- Automation accelerates fixes but increases chance of human-less merges; mitigated with approval and short manual windows.
- Preferring rollforward reduces churn but may leave transient customer-facing anomalies; risk appetite is set per severity.
